name: Monotonic stack
purpose: Find a next greater, next smaller, or nearest value efficiently.
mechanism: Scan once and keep unresolved indices in monotonic order. Pop an index only when the current value resolves it; storing indices preserves both the value and its distance.
complexity: O(n): every index is pushed once and popped at most once.
pitfalls: Store indices, not just values, when distance matters.
Use a while-loop for multiple newly resolved items.

name: Monotonic deque
purpose: Maintain the maximum or minimum of a sliding window in linear time.
mechanism: Remove expired indices from the front and dominated candidates from the back before adding the current index.
pitfalls: Evict by index before reading the window answer.
Keep indices so expiry is unambiguous.

name: Backtracking
purpose: Explore combinations, permutations, and constrained choices.
mechanism: Choose, recurse, then undo exactly that choice before trying the next branch.
complexity: Usually exponential; state the output-sensitive cost.
pitfalls: Always pop to restore the path.
Store results with [...path], because arrays are references.

name: Two heaps
purpose: Maintain a running median or split a stream around a boundary.
mechanism: Keep the lower half in a max-heap and upper half in a min-heap. Insert, transfer the boundary, then rebalance so the max-heap has the same number or one more.
complexity: O(log n) insertion and O(1) median.
pitfalls: Average both heap tops for an even count.

name: Quickselect
purpose: Find a kth element without fully sorting.
mechanism: Partition around a pivot and continue only in the partition containing the target index.
complexity: Expected O(n) with randomized pivots; O(n²) remains possible in the worst case.
pitfalls: Convert kth-largest to the correct zero-based target index.
Randomize the pivot to avoid predictable bad input.

name: Binary search on answer
purpose: Find a minimum or maximum feasible threshold.
mechanism: Binary-search the range of possible answers and use a greedy feasibility check for each candidate.
complexity: Often O(n log S), where S is the answer range.
pitfalls: Set bounds from the problem, such as max item through total sum.
For a minimum feasible value, a feasible mid searches lower.

name: Two pointers
purpose: Search sorted arrays or shrink and expand an array range.
mechanism: Move the left or right pointer according to whether the current value is below or above the target.
complexity: Usually O(n) after any required sort.
pitfalls: Skip adjacent duplicates for unique 3-sum results.
Account for the O(n log n) sorting cost.

name: Negative marking
purpose: Find duplicates or missing values in a [1,n] array with constant extra space.
mechanism: Use abs(value)-1 as an index and negate the value there. A value already negative indicates a repeat.
complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
pitfalls: Use Math.abs before calculating the index.
Mention that the input is mutated.

name: Merge intervals
mechanism: Sort by start, compare each interval to the latest merged interval, and extend its end when current.start <= last.end.
complexity: O(n log n) due to sorting.
pitfalls: Use max of the two end values so a containing interval is preserved.
Do not compare only with the previous unmerged interval.
